questions.questionText: Your team is stuck waiting on your sign-off to move forward. They've got the context, they just need a yes or no from you. What do you do?
questions.followupPrompt: If you had to pick, would you move things forward now or wait for more context first?

answers.answerText: Approve it and keep things moving.
Get a quick read from the team, then make the call.
Review the options before giving a final answer.
Hold off until I have the full picture.

questions.questionText: You're mid-sprint and you realize the direction needs to change. Your team already started building. How do you handle it?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you pivot immediately, or pause to validate the change before moving?

answers.answerText: Redirect the team right away and keep shipping.
Dig into why it changed, then reset priorities with the team.
Push back and try to protect the original scope.
Pause the sprint until the new direction is clear.

questions.questionText: One of your team members in a completely different timezone sends you a Slack message. You're in the middle of something. What do you do?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you reply quickly today, or keep it for a scheduled sync?

answers.answerText: Reply as soon as I see it.
Respond when I come up for air.
Batch my replies and respond later in the day.
Address it during my next sync or standup.

questions.questionText: It's Monday morning. You've got three different projects that all need attention this week, and your calendar is already packed. How do you approach it?
questions.followupPrompt: Do you usually context-switch across work, or focus deeply on one item first?

answers.answerText: Jump between all three and keep everything moving.
Decide what's most urgent and start there.
Block my calendar and follow a plan for the week.
Go deep on one project at a time until it's done.

questions.questionText: You're on a team call and someone pushes back hard on your approach. They think there's a better way. How do you respond?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you push your approach, or work toward a shared middle ground?

answers.answerText: Back my decision and move forward.
Explain my reasoning and give them room to make their case.
Look for a compromise that works for both sides.
Give them ownership if their idea is better.

questions.questionText: Your team is remote and spread across 3 timezones. Everyone's working different hours. How do you prefer to stay aligned with them?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you rather keep a daily pulse, or communicate mainly on scheduled cadence?

answers.answerText: Stay in the channels and keep a pulse on things all day.
One daily standup or sync to cover priorities.
A weekly recap to review what shipped and what's next.
Async updates only when there's something worth sharing.

questions.questionText: You're working on a task and hit a wall. Your lead is offline and probably won't reply for a few hours. How do you handle it?

questions.questionText: You're halfway done with a deliverable and the brief changes out of nowhere. New direction, different expectations. What's your move?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you rework immediately, or ask clarifying questions first?

answers.answerText: Pivot and start reworking right away.
Ask clarifying questions before changing anything.

questions.followupPrompt: Do you tend to context-switch, or go deep on one critical task at a time?

answers.answerText: Context-switch and chip away at all of them.

Stick to the schedule I already set for the week.
Block out distractions and deep-work on one at a time.

questions.questionText: Your Team Builder sends feedback on a deliverable and you genuinely disagree with their direction. What do you do?
questions.followupPrompt: Would you push back directly, or work toward a version that meets both sides?

answers.answerText: Push back and explain why my approach works better.

Suggest a version that meets both sides halfway.
Go with their feedback, they know their business best.

questions.followupPrompt: Would you keep a daily update rhythm, or send updates mainly when progress is ready?

answers.answerText: Quick Slack updates throughout the day.
A short daily update, async or live.
A weekly summary with what's done and what's next.
Share updates when there's real progress to show.
